rows.stem: Select saponification reaction from the following :
rows.solution:
Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of an ester: heating an ester with sodium hydroxide gives the sodium salt of the carboxylic acid (a soap, when the acid is a long-chain fatty acid) and an alcohol. Ethyl ethanoate and sodium hydroxide give sodium ethanoate and ethanol:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5 + NaOH \rightarrow CH_3COONa + C_2H_5OH}\)

Of the other choices, one is the oxidation of an alcohol to a carboxylic acid by alkaline potassium permanganate, one is the decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate to methane, and one is the reaction of ethanol with sodium. (That last choice prints the product as \(\mathrm{C_2H_5COONa}\); ethanol and sodium actually give sodium ethoxide, \(\mathrm{C_2H_5ONa}\), and hydrogen. It is not saponification either way.)

This is option (C) \(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5 + NaOH \longrightarrow CH_3COONa + C_2H_5OH}\).

rows.stem: United Nations Environment Programme forged an agreement to
rows.solution:
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers, deplete the ozone layer. In 1987 the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) forged an agreement to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels, so that the depletion of the ozone layer would be checked.

This is option (D) reduce CFC production.

rows.stem: Which one of the following statements is TRUE for Hydra, Amoeba and Spirogyra ?
rows.solution:
Amoeba is unicellular while Hydra and Spirogyra are multicellular, so neither of the statements about the number of cells holds for all three. What they share is asexual reproduction: Amoeba divides by binary fission, Hydra reproduces by budding (and regeneration), and Spirogyra breaks into fragments (fragmentation), each fragment growing into a new filament.

This is option (D) They reproduce asexually.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Oxides of metals show basic characters.

**Reason (R) :** Oxides of metals react with acid to form salt and water.
rows.context: Q. 17 to 20 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R), answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Metal oxides such as copper oxide and magnesium oxide are basic oxides, so the Assertion is true. They react with acids to give a salt and water, for example

\(\mathrm{CuO + 2HCl \rightarrow CuCl_2 + H_2O}\)

so the Reason is true. Reacting with an acid to give a salt and water is exactly what makes an oxide basic, so the Reason explains the Assertion.

The Reason is true and explains the Assertion. This is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** In human beings, males have ‘XX’ sex chromosomes and females have ‘XY’ sex chromosomes.

**Reason (R) :** Sex of the child is determined at the time of fertilisation when male and female gamete fuse to form a zygote.
rows.context: Q. 17 to 20 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R), answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
In human beings females have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes, XX, while males have a mismatched pair, XY. The Assertion states it the other way round, so the Assertion is false.

The sex of the child is decided at fertilisation: every egg carries an X chromosome, and if it fuses with a sperm carrying X the zygote (XX) develops into a girl, while a sperm carrying Y gives a zygote (XY) that develops into a boy. So the Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Receptors are usually located in our sense organs and perceive a particular stimulus.

**Reason (R) :** Different sense organs have different receptors for detecting stimuli.
rows.context: Q. 17 to 20 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R), answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Receptors are specialised tips of nerve cells, usually located in the sense organs (eye, ear, nose, tongue and skin), and they detect information from the environment, so the Assertion is true. Different sense organs carry different receptors, for example the gustatory receptors of the tongue detect taste and the olfactory receptors of the nose detect smell, so the Reason is also true. But the Reason does not explain why receptors are located in the sense organs.

Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.stem:
When a few drops of Barium chloride solution are added to an aqueous solution of Sodium sulphate, a white precipitate is obtained.

(a) Write balanced chemical equation for the reaction involved.

(b) What is the other name of this precipitation reaction ? Why is it called so ?
rows.solution:
(a) Barium chloride reacts with sodium sulphate to give a white precipitate of barium sulphate, leaving sodium chloride in solution:

\(\mathrm{BaCl_2(aq) + Na_2SO_4(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}\)

(b) It is also called a double displacement reaction. It is called so because the two reactants exchange their ions: barium pairs with sulphate and sodium pairs with chloride.

rows.stem:
Define the terms biodegradable and non-biodegradable substance. Classify the following items into these two categories :

Newspapers, Glass bottles, Polythene bags, Vegetable peels
rows.solution:
Biodegradable substances are those that are broken down into simpler substances by biological processes, that is, by the action of decomposers such as bacteria and fungi.

Non-biodegradable substances are those that are not broken down by biological processes; they persist in the environment for a long time.

Biodegradable: newspapers, vegetable peels.

Non-biodegradable: glass bottles, polythene bags.

rows.stem: Write electronic configuration of Sodium (At. No.11) and Oxygen (At. No. 8) and show the formation of the ionic compound obtained when these two elements combine. Name anion and cation present in the compound.
rows.solution:
Electronic configurations: sodium (11) is 2, 8, 1 and oxygen (8) is 2, 6.

Sodium loses its one valence electron to reach the stable configuration 2, 8, and oxygen gains two electrons to complete its octet, 2, 8. So two sodium atoms each give one electron to one oxygen atom:

\(\mathrm{2Na \rightarrow 2Na^+ + 2e^-}\)

\(\mathrm{O + 2e^- \rightarrow O^{2-}}\)

In the electron-dot diagram, draw each sodium atom with one dot (its valence electron) and the oxygen atom with six crosses. Curved arrows carry the two dots onto the oxygen. The product is written as two sodium ions, \(\mathrm{[Na^+]_2}\), beside the oxide ion in a bracket with its eight electrons (six crosses and two dots) and the charge \(2-\):

\(\mathrm{2Na^+ + O^{2-} \rightarrow Na_2O}\) (sodium oxide)

The cation is the sodium ion, \(\mathrm{Na^+}\), and the anion is the oxide ion, \(\mathrm{O^{2-}}\).

rows.stem: Write the main difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration. State the pathway which is common for both. Write the overall chemical equation of aerobic respiration and mention the site where this process occurs inside the cells.
rows.solution:
Main difference: aerobic respiration uses oxygen, while anaerobic respiration takes place in the absence of oxygen. (Aerobic respiration breaks glucose down completely to carbon dioxide and water and releases much more energy; anaerobic respiration gives ethanol and carbon dioxide in yeast, or lactic acid in our muscles.)

The common pathway is glycolysis: in the cytoplasm, glucose (a six-carbon molecule) is broken down into pyruvate (a three-carbon molecule).

Glucose \(\xrightarrow{\text{in cytoplasm}}\) Pyruvate \(\xrightarrow{\text{presence of oxygen}}\) Carbon dioxide + Water + Energy

As a single overall equation:

\(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O + energy}\)

The breakdown of pyruvate using oxygen takes place in the mitochondria.

rows.stem: List three advantages of parallel circuits in domestic wiring.
rows.solution:
Any three:

1. Each appliance has its own switch, so each one can be switched on and off separately as required.

2. If one appliance stops working because of a defect, all the other appliances keep working.

3. Each appliance gets the full (equal) potential difference of the supply and draws the current it needs.

4. The total resistance of a parallel circuit is less than the smallest individual resistance, so the circuit can supply the current each appliance needs.

rows.stem:
(a) What is puberty ? Write any two changes that occur in boys during early teenage years.

(b) List two functions performed by testis in human males.

Mention one role each of (i) Vas deferens, (ii) Seminal Vesicle (iii) Urethra and (iv) Scrotum in human male reproductive system.
rows.solution:
(a) Puberty is the period in early teenage years when the rate of general body growth begins to slow down and the reproductive tissues begin to mature.

Changes in boys (any two): thick new hair grows on the face (beard and moustache); the voice begins to crack; the penis occasionally begins to enlarge and become erect.

(b) Functions of the testis: it forms the sperms (male germ cells), and it secretes the hormone testosterone, which regulates sperm formation and brings about the changes in boys at puberty.

Roles:

(i) Vas deferens: delivers the sperms from the testes to the urethra.

(ii) Seminal vesicle: adds its secretion to the sperms, which provides them nutrition and makes their transport easier.

(iii) Urethra: the common passage for both sperms and urine.

(iv) Scrotum: holds the testes outside the abdominal cavity, providing the lower temperature needed for sperm formation.

rows.stem:
(a) Write two functions each of the following parts in human female reproductive system :

(i) Ovary

(ii) Oviduct

(iii) Uterus

(b) Describe the structure and function of placenta.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) Ovary: it produces the female germ cells (eggs), releasing one egg every month; it also secretes hormones such as oestrogen.

(ii) Oviduct (fallopian tube): it carries the egg from the ovary towards the uterus, and it is the site of fertilisation.

(iii) Uterus: the fertilised egg (zygote) is implanted in its lining, and it nourishes and protects the developing embryo until birth.

(b) Structure: the placenta is a special disc-like tissue embedded in the uterine wall and connected to the embryo. It has villi on the embryo's side, and blood spaces on the mother's side which surround the villi.

Function: it provides a large surface area for glucose and oxygen to pass from the mother's blood to the embryo, and for the waste substances produced by the embryo to pass into the mother's blood for removal.
